posts.author: JazzChicken
posts.body:
Hello to all you cool cats!
I am a loooong returning user of RPG maker and as such I am incredibly rusty and out of the loop  I recently ran a charity stream raising money for the RSPCA to prevent cruelty to animals, and my highest donation reward for £100 was the viewer can force me to create my own game.
I had TWO people donate £100! So now I must make 2 games
One will be a platformer on game maker and one will be an RPG maker game as I dabbled a bit back in the RPG Maker 2000 and XP days.
I checked out and purchased MV as its more modern and seems more user friendly, but I had some questions before I go hunting through a pile of forums to find anything that helps.
Q1) The sprites are very tiny and squashed with big heads. XP supported sprites of any size. Does MV also allow sprites of any size? Or will I have to split big sprites into multiple smaller sprites and have them move together as one?
If it does. How would I create larger sprites? Do they need to be a particular canvas size or can the canvas be whatever size?
Q2) The sprite animation looks to be just 3 frames. Is it possible to increase the frame limit per direction? This is just to see if I can make smoother animations or not.
Q3) I've never been a fan of the battle mechanics (especially the side on battle with tiny heroes and giant enemies)
Is it possible to create a tactical battle mechanic with RPG maker MV? Similar to Breath of fire and Shining force?
I'm guessing I may need a number of scripts or plug ins.
Q4) They appear to have removed the ability to layer images from the chipsets. Yet when I had a little play with MV some images automatically layered over other images.
Does MV support multiple layers? Or is it just the one layer?
Also is there a way of knowing which images in the chipset will layer over the top? As I noticed some layer and some don't. Even with transparent backgrounds.
Thats pretty much all for now. Anything else I will fumble around this website and try to find.
Mostly just wanted to say hello to everyone and see how much the community has changed over the years  It used to be a highly toxic place back in the early 2000s

posts.author: wiffle88
posts.body:
Q1) The sprites are very tiny and squashed with big heads. XP supported sprites of any size. Does MV also allow sprites of any size? Or will I have to split big sprites into multiple smaller sprites and have them move together as one?
A1) From the RPG Maker MV Help file:
Characters (img/characters)Images shown for the characters on the map.
The size for a character image can be changed freely (normally 48x48), and consist of 4 directions (down, left, right, up) and 3 patterns for a total of 12 patterns that will be arranged in the provided order. A file for 1 character will be arranged into 2 rows and 4 columns equaling 8 images. The size of the character will be calculated using 1/12 of the width and 1/8 of the height of this file. Moreover, characters will be shown 6 pixels above tile so that they appear more natural when on top of buildings.
It is possible treat 1 character as 1 file by including "$" at the beginning of the file name.
Including a "!" at the beginning of the file name will prevent the image from being shifted 6 pixels and will no longer appear half transparent by bush elements. This is primarily used for objects found in the map such as doors and treasure chests.
It is also possible to use the "$" and "!" special characters together.
-------------------------------------
Q2) The sprite animation looks to be just 3 frames. Is it possible to increase the frame limit per direction? This is just to see if I can make smoother animations or not.
A2) By default, no.  However there are plugins that do this.  One that comes to mind is
this one.
-------------------------------------
Q3) I've never been a fan of the battle mechanics (especially the side on battle with tiny heroes and giant enemies)
Is it possible to create a tactical battle mechanic with RPG maker MV? Similar to Breath of fire and Shining force?
I'm guessing I may need a number of scripts or plug ins.
A3) Yes, there are several plugins out there that can change the battle system and create on-map battle systems.  Though most will require some amount of setup.
-------------------------------------
Q4) They appear to have removed the ability to layer images from the chipsets. Yet when I had a little play with MV some images automatically layered over other images.
Does MV support multiple layers? Or is it just the one layer?
Also is there a way of knowing which images in the chipset will layer over the top? As I noticed some layer and some don't. Even with transparent backgrounds.
A4) Not sure what you mean by chipset, but I believe they removed some of the layering ability from earlier RPG Makers.  The following is from the RPG Maker MV helpfile:
Upper Layer Tile Special Specifications
You can layer 2 different types on the upper maps B-E.
* When layering a 3rd tile, the 1st upper tile will disappear.
* When the 3rd tile layered is the same as the 2nd tile, the first tile will not disappear.
* Only the upper left B tile can erase all upper tiles.
When a passable tile and an impassable tile are layered, the effect of the tile layered last takes priority.
* Even when a passable ☆ tile is on the bottom, the tile with the ☆ will be displayed on top.
* When a passable ☆ tile is layered, the impassable tile's effect will take priority.
Lower Layer Tile Special SpecificationsAmongst the tiles that are displayed in the [A] tab of the Tile Palette, those items found in [A2] in the tileset properties are divided into [Base] (tiles 1 to 4 from the left, or the left half) and [Decoration] tiles (tiles 5 to 8 from the left, or the right half). Decoration tiles can be placed on top of base tiles.
However, for those [Tilesets] which have their [Mode] set to [World Type] in the tileset properties, when placing a decoration tile that is stacked on a 2nd or 4th base tile, the base tile will change either the 1st or 3rd base tile.
A plugin that could help a lot of layering is
this.
You can find the RPG Maker MV helpfile
here
.  I also find the
RPG Maker MV/MZ Script Call List
to be invaluable.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
JazzChicken said:
It looks like you can indeed layer a lot of stuff like before.
Click to expand...
Manual layer control was removed after RMXP and only reintroduced again with MZ.
The three makers VX, VXA and MV all use automatic layer control (which is optional for MZ as well).
This means that all A-Tiles go to the bottom layer and all B to E tiles go to the upper layer (or upper two layers for MV).
Additionally, you can use a decorative event with a tile from B-E on top of those two or three map layers.
